Hi Alex / Neha — quick note from ops on what usually causes the behavior Alex saw and a couple of fixes.

Root causes we see:
- Forwarded invites: Gmail can drop explicit timezone metadata when an invite is forwarded or when the forwarding client strips the TZ field, leading the recipient's calendar to show a "floating" time.
- Floating events: If an event is created without a TZ, Google will display it relative to the calendar's default, which can be wrong across DST boundaries.
- Client differences: Outlook/Gmail/Apple handle ICS TZ parameters differently.

Workarounds/fixes:
1) Create the event with an explicit TZ property in the ICS (i.e., DTSTART;TZID=Europe/Paris:20260317T173000). I attached a sanitized ICS you can send directly (invite-event.ics).
2) Include the UTC time in the event description to give a canonical reference (2026-03-17 16:30 UTC = 17:30 CET).
3) Use Google Calendar "Add to calendar" links with tz=Europe/Paris param for browser invites: https://calendar.google.com/calendar/render?action=TEMPLATE&text=Redwood+Demo&dates=20260317T163000Z/20260317T170000Z&ctz=Europe/Paris
4) If someone forwards the invite, ask them to forward the original invite email rather than the calendar UI event. That preserves the ICS.

I'll attach the ICS now. Neha — if you send the ICS as the new invite and include the UTC line in the body, that should resolve Alex's view.

Marcus Lin
